title: Field pilot outcomes, prioritized roadmap, and decision log — Acme retail assistant
body:
Executive summary:

This doc summarizes the 3-week field pilot run for Acme Retail’s in-store assistant (user-facing help + shelf lookup), captures the technical and business outcomes, and provides a prioritized roadmap + concrete next steps to move from pilot -> production. The pilot met the core correctness and latency goals for peak in-store interactions but surfaced clear reliability and cost-optimization work before a full rollout.

Objectives and scope:
- Primary objective: Validate that Redwood’s inference stack can deliver sub-300ms p50 response for short-form in-store queries (<= 64 tokens) and maintain acceptable hallucination rate (< 2% on curated intents) while being cost-competitive with Acme’s target of <$0.005 per query.
- Scope: 3-week live pilot at 4 stores, heavy focus on FAQ retrieval + dynamic inventory checks, limited payment/PII flows (out of scope).
- Participants: small cohort of store associates and beta customers; internal success metrics instrumented via Redwood Console and custom Analytics events.

POC setup (quick recap):
- Model: open-weights Llama-2-13b quantized variant (v0.3-opt) with prompt templates tuned for Acme taxonomy.
- Runtime: Redwood Dedicated (dev pool) — 4x A100 equiv (shared across stores via smart-routing), autoscaling disabled for pilot to keep metrics stable.
- Optimizations enabled: KV prefix caching for repeated item lookups, continuous batching window = 12ms, top-k=40 sampling for discovery queries.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost tracing, per-request latency and KV cache hit/miss, hallucination annotation flow in the app (manual QA).

Key results (metrics):
- Latency: p50 = 220ms, p95 = 490ms (for <=64-token queries) under pilot traffic pattern (avg concurrency 6).
- Throughput: steady-state 85 qps across the pool during peak 10–11am window.
- Cost: estimated infra cost (hosted-equivalent) = ~$0.0048/query (including model and networking). Edge-case long answers (200+ tokens) pushed average per-interaction token count up and cost spikes observed.
- Quality: curated intent accuracy = 94%, hallucination incidents flagged by QA = 1.7% (mostly on ambiguous product synonyms).
- Reliability: 3 transient API timeouts during week 2 correlated with a node firmware reboot in the provider region; automatic fallback to smaller variant worked but increased p95 to ~700ms for a 12-minute window.

Qualitative feedback (from store associates and product):
- Pros: responses feel natural and helpful; KV caching meaningfully sped up repeated inventory lookups (per-associate feedback).
- Cons: edge-case handling for multi-step returns/questions needs more deterministic tool-calling to avoid incorrect suggestions.
- UX ask: allow associates to toggle between "concise" and "explain" response modes.

Technical findings and recommendations (high-level):
1) KV caching is effective but requires warm strategies for cold-started SKUs. Recommendation: pre-warm cache for top-200 SKUs per store during morning sync.
2) Batching window 12ms is a good sweet spot for pilot concurrency, but for broader rollout we should explore dynamic batching by route to keep p50 < 250ms while increasing throughput.
3) Quantized model variant meets quality bar; however some ambiguous-entity hallucinations indicate the need for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with stricter grounding for inventory answers. Short-term: integrate lightweight RAG via embeddings index for SKU descriptions.
4) Fallback policy worked but increased latency. Recommendation: implement fast-fail detection and prefer regional routing to warm standby nodes before falling back to smaller model variants.

Deployment options and tradeoffs (short list):
- Option A — Hosted incremental: fast to ship, easiest ops, but less data isolation and harder to guarantee region-specific latency for all stores. Best for: feature validation in more stores.
- Option B — Dedicated reserved pool per-region: predictable latency and lower per-query cost at scale, supports guaranteed throughput SLAs. Best for: production rollout across ~100+ stores.
- Option C — Private (VPC/or on-prem): required only if Acme wants full control over PII and network egress; higher ops and license cost. Best for: regulated or security-sensitive expansions.

Recommendation (short): Start with Option A for a 6–8 week staged rollout to 20 pilot stores to gather more traffic patterns and tune batching/caching. Parallel work: prepare Dedicated proposal for Q3 commit (capacity sizing + price book) so we can migrate without feature regressions. If legal requires, start Private onboarding checklist in parallel (low priority until >1M monthly queries).

Prioritized next steps (concrete, with owners & ETA):
1) Pre-warm plan for top-200 SKUs per store — owner: Ethan Patel — ETA: 2 weeks. (NOTE: need a small job to seed KV cache; ticket JIRA-4521)
2) Implement RAG pipeline with lightweight embeddings index for SKU descriptions — owner: Rui Gomez — ETA: 3 weeks (proof-of-concept on dev cluster).
3) Dynamic batching by route (experiment) — owner: Jordan Lee — ETA: 4 weeks. Goal: reduce p95 by 15% at scale.
4) Run 20-store staged rollout under Hosted mode — owner: Maya Chen / Acme PM — ETA: start in 2 weeks, monitor 4-week window.
5) Draft Dedicated capacity + pricing proposal for Acme — owner: Solutions ENG lead — ETA: 6 weeks (deliverable: capacity estimate + 12-month commit pricing).
6) Ops runbook updates (fallbacks + rollback) and SRE oncall playbook — owner: SRE team (Sofia) — ETA: 3 weeks.

Decision log (historical, short):
- 2026-02-05: Chose Llama-2-13b quant variant for best latency/quality tradeoff (reason: match Acme's accuracy target while keeping memory profile small enough for Dedicated pool).
- 2026-02-15: Disabled autoscale during pilot to keep metrics comparable across stores (reason: make p95 comparisons deterministic).
- 2026-03-03: Approved small fallback to smaller variant after observation of node reboot (reason: maintain availability).

Risks and mitigations:
- Hallucination risk on ambiguous SKUs: mitigate with RAG + stronger grounding and a conservative threshold for asserting facts.
- Cost overruns if average tokens per query increase: mitigate with prompting to encourage concise responses, enforce generation limits, and enable per-route token caps.
- Region reliability: add regional warm standby and a fast-fail detection to avoid long p95 spikes.

Estimated costs (ballpark, text):
- Pilot (3 weeks) measured infra = ~$5k (covered by demo budget).
- 20-store Hosted staged rollout (4 weeks): projected infra = ~$25k; expected cost-per-query remains ~0.0045–0.005 depending on tokenization.
- Dedicated reserve sizing for 100 stores (steady-state): estimated monthly = ~$35k–$48k (depending on burst profile and instance type). Exact sizing requires traffic profile from staged rollout.

Acceptance criteria to promote to production:
- p50 <= 250ms and p95 <= 600ms under target concurrency for each region.
- Hallucination <= 1.5% on expanded QA set (1000 cases).
- Cost per query <= $0.005 at 95th percentile expected traffic.
- Runbook and rollback playbook validated with SRE tabletop exercise.

Close-out checklist for pilot: (quick)
- [ ] Complete pre-warm job and confirm cache hit rate improvement >= 30%
- [ ] Ship RAG POC and measure hallucination delta
- [ ] Create Dedicated sizing proposal and internal price proposal
- [ ] Update runbooks + schedule SRE tabletop
- [ ] Product decision on "concise/explain" response toggle UX

Notes / open questions (to discuss with Acme PM in next readout):
- Should we allow associates to opt into longer responses (tradeoff cost vs. satisfaction)?
- Legal: any non-PII retention constraints that would force Private deployment earlier?
- What SLA does Acme want for peak-store hours (weekend afternoons)?

Attachments / artifacts to review:
- Pilot telemetry dashboard (Console link): CONFLUENCE-1234
- QA incident log (spreadsheet): JIRA-4521
- Runbook draft: github.com/redwood-inference/acme-pilot/blob/main/runbook.md

Immediate asks for next readout:
- Approval to run 20-store hosted staged rollout (need signoff from Acme PM + Commercial).
- Budget approval for RAG PoC compute (small dev cluster).

TODOs (internal):
- Add a short one-pager for Commercial that describes Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoffs (owner: Maya).
- Ensure legal reviews data retention notes next week (owner: Sofia).

-- end of doc --
